title: ProductWebBench: Evaluating Website Continuity Beyond Task Completion
abstract: arXiv:2610.31118v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Frontend coding agents are usually graded on one question: did the requested target get built. Real engineering changes carry a second obligation, because the rest of the site has to keep working. We call that second obligation website continuity, and introduce ProductWebBench, a benchmark that scores both on living frontend repositories: 320 Change tasks over existing code and 80 long-horizon Build tasks. Every task freezes a repository snapshot, staged requirements, browser evidence and deterministic checks before evaluation, and enters only once a reference passes every check and plausible-wrong ones fail. A simulated user reveals the requirements one stage at a time, and every check cleared earlier stays armed for the rest of the run. translated_title: ProductWebBench：超越任务完成度的网站连续性评估
translated_abstract: 前端编码智能体通常只用一个问题来评判：被要求的目标是否被构建出来。而真实的工程变更还承载着第二项义务——网站其余部分必须保持正常运作。我们将这项第二义务称为“网站连续性”，并推出 ProductWebBench，一个在真实前端仓库上同时对两者进行评分的基准：包含 320 个针对现有代码的变更任务和 80 个长周期构建任务。每个任务在评估前都会冻结仓库快照、分阶段需求、浏览器证据和确定性检查，并且只有当参考实现通过全部检查、而似是而非的错误实现无法通过时，任务才会被收录。模拟用户会逐个阶段揭示需求，且此前已通过的所有检查在整个运行过程中持续生效。来自 13 个模型的 8,737 次运行表明，两者会分道扬镳：在通过所有“请求工作”检查的变更任务运行中，仍有 28.2% 未通过连续性检查——出现空白路由、水平溢出、控制台报错等问题。
tldr: 该论文提出 ProductWebBench 基准，首次在真实前端仓库上评估“网站连续性”（即代码变更后网站其余部分是否仍正常运行），并发现即使通过所有任务要求检查的变更运行中，仍有 28.2% 会破坏网站的其他功能。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces ProductWebBench, a benchmark that evaluates "website continuity" — whether the rest of a site keeps working after frontend changes — showing that 28.2% of Change-task runs passing all requested-work checks still break the site.
